verdicts.name: star is sixfold at every s tested, one state per sector
verdicts.detail: S_z = +5/2..-5/2, a single S=5/2 multiplet (Lieb-Mattis 1962, |nA-nB|=5)

verdicts.name: no single sector can return 2 from this Hamiltonian
verdicts.detail: every sector's ground state is non-degenerate, so no threshold yields 2

verdicts.name: a genuine star goes TWOFOLD when the off-diagonal is written J not 2J
verdicts.detail: deg 2 in sectors S_z = +2.5 and -2.5, at every s tested

verdicts.name: and Ising-only does the same, on the same correct graph
verdicts.detail: so twofold is a statement about the Hamiltonian, not about the graph

verdicts.name: a GENUINE star under easy-plane anisotropy also sits at S_z = +/-1/2
verdicts.detail: 35 of 35 configurations give deg 2 in sectors S_z = +0.5 and -0.5, so S_z does NOT separate a broken operator from a wrong graph

verdicts.name: the S_z discriminator sent on 30 August is therefore RETRACTED
verdicts.detail: easy-axis puts a broken star at +/-5/2 and easy-plane puts it at +/-1/2, so the sector alone is not a test; the degeneracy across N below is the one that works

verdicts.name: twofold appears immediately below isotropy, not only far from it
verdicts.detail: xy = 1.999 down to 0.5 all give deg 2 in sectors [1,6]; xy = 2.0 exactly still gives 6, so a builder that returned 2 for every xy would fail this

verdicts.name: N=8 and N=9 separate the two causes on his own controls
verdicts.detail: isotropic gives N=7:6, N=8:7, N=9:8; anisotropic gives 2 at every N

verdicts.name: the s=0 -> 0.01 turn he reports is a RANK CHANGE
verdicts.detail: deg 10 at s=0 (S=5/2 + S=3/2, the leaf detaches) and 6 immediately after

verdicts.name: a 4-against-3 graph really does put its twofold at S_z = +/-1/2
verdicts.detail: chain deg 2 in sectors n_up 3 and 4, i.e. S_z = +0.5 and -0.5, at all five s

verdicts.name: an HONEST s -> 0 produces no sharp turn in our manifold
verdicts.detail: theta1 = 0.0016 rad between s = 1e-9 and s = 0.01

verdicts.name: the falsy zero DOES produce a turn, about 100x larger
verdicts.detail: theta1 = 0.1658 rad if s=0 is silently rebuilt as 1.0

verdicts.name: but it does NOT reach his 0.819, so it is not the whole story
verdicts.detail: 0.1658 against his 0.819; the gap is left open rather than explained away

verdicts.name: our sixfold manifold rotates RIGIDLY: all six angles equal
verdicts.detail: spread across the six angles is 2.15e-10 and 1.33e-15, so theta1 equals the largest

verdicts.name: theta1 = Omega forces every other angle to zero, which rigid rotation forbids
verdicts.detail: his chain 0.065/0.046 = 1.413 = sqrt(2), two equal angles; his star theta1 = Omega = 0.819, so one angle is 0.819 and the rest are zero

verdicts.name: RETRACTED twofold does NOT imply |nA - nB| = 1
verdicts.detail: C_7 is not bipartite and is twofold at 4 of 5 s

verdicts.name: and a connected non-bipartite graph does it at every s
verdicts.detail: triangle with pendants: not bipartite, twofold at all five

verdicts.name: REFUTED an opposite exchange sign does not explain his 2
verdicts.detail: sign-flipped star is EIGHTfold (S = 7/2), not twofold

verdicts.name: CONTROL a CONNECTED mis-built star is caught
verdicts.detail: one leaf re-hung: |nA-nB| = 3 and deg = 4, both differ from the star; the old control only caught DISCONNECTED graphs and would have passed this

verdicts.name: CONTROL the isotropic arm reproduces the theorem it cites
verdicts.detail: deg = |nA-nB| + 1 on both bipartite graphs; a builder with the wrong sign fails here

verdicts.name: CONTROL s=0 detaches the edge and is excluded on purpose
verdicts.detail: at s=0 the degeneracy is 10, not 6, which is why the grid starts above it
